title: Funerary Inscriptions, Part One
subtitle: Five epitaphs from Autun, Alise-Sainte-Reine, and Saint-Marcel — ANDEDASETI, MARKOM, MONI.
objectives: Translate the formula ANDEDASETI ("he set up").
Recognize MARKOM ("horse") and MONI ("memorial") in funerary contexts.
Read five complete funerary inscriptions from Gaul.
Parse personal names and patronymics in epitaphs.

sections.heading: Funerary formulae
sections.body:
Gaulish funerary inscriptions follow consistent patterns. The most common formula is:

X [patronymic] ANDEDASETI Y MONI

"X [son of Y] set up this memorial."

Variants include:

X DEDEMIT — "X gave (this)"
X IEVRV — "X dedicated (this)"
X AVVOT — "X vowed (this)"

The key verb is ANDEDASETI ("he set up"), the preterite of a verb meaning "to set up" or "to erect". The prefix ANDE- intensifies or marks completion.

sections.heading: Inscription 1: Autun
sections.body:
Here is a complete funerary inscription from Autun (ancient Augustodunum), 1st century CE:

SEGOMĀROS VILONEOS ANDEDASETI MONI

Parsing:
SEGOMĀROS — nominative singular, personal name, "great in victory"
VILONEOS — genitive singular, patronymic, "of Viloneos"
ANDEDASETI — 3rd singular preterite, "set up"
MONI — accusative singular, "memorial" (cognate with Latin monumentum)

Translation: "Segomaros son of Viloneos set up this memorial."

sections.heading: Inscription 2: Alise-Sainte-Reine
sections.body:
From Alise-Sainte-Reine (ancient Alesia, site of Vercingetorix's last stand), 1st century CE:

DAGOMĀROS ANDEVDDOS DEDEMIT MARKOM

Parsing:
DAGOMĀROS — nominative singular, "good and great"
ANVEDDOS — nominative singular, personal name (etymology uncertain)
DEDEMIT — 3rd singular preterite, "gave" or "dedicated"
MARKOM — accusative singular, "horse" (cognate with Latin marcus, borrowed into Gaulish)

Translation: "Dagomaros Andevddos gave (this) horse."

Note: MARKOM here may refer to a carved image of a horse, a votive offering, or a symbolic representation. Horse imagery was common in Gaulish funerary art.

sections.heading: Inscription 3: Saint-Marcel
sections.body:
From Saint-Marcel (near Argentomagus), 1st century CE:

ATEPOMĀROS SEGOMARI ANDEDASETI

Parsing:
ATEPOMĀROS — nominative singular, "very great"
SEGOMĀRI — genitive singular, patronymic, "of Segomaros"
ANDEDASETI — "set up"

Translation: "Atepomaros son of Segomaros set up (this)."

sections.heading: Inscription 4: Autun
sections.body:
A second inscription from Autun, 1st century CE:

NERTOMĀROS DVBNORIGI MONI BRIXTOM

Parsing:
NERTOMĀROS — nominative singular, "great in strength"
DVBNORIGI — genitive or dative singular, patronymic, "of Dubnorix" or "to Dubnorix"
MONI — accusative singular, "memorial"
BRIXTOM — accusative singular, "magic" or "spell" (etymology disputed; may refer to a protective charm carved on the stone)

Translation: "Nertomaros (son of) Dubnorix (set up) this memorial (with) magic."

sections.heading: Inscription 5: Alise-Sainte-Reine
sections.body:
A third from Alise-Sainte-Reine, 1st century CE:

VERCINGETORIX ANDEDASETI

Parsing:
VERCINGETORIX — nominative singular, "king over warriors" (the famous name, here on a funerary stone — not necessarily the same Vercingetorix who fought Caesar, but the name lived on)
ANDEDASETI — "set up"

Translation: "Vercingetorix set up (this)."

items.answer: "He set up" — 3rd singular preterite, common in funerary inscriptions.
"Horse" — cognate with Latin marcus, possibly referring to a carved horse or votive offering.
"Segomaros son of Viloneos set up this memorial."
"Magic" or "spell" — possibly a protective charm. Etymology disputed.
NERTOMAROS (nom. sg., "great in strength") DVBNORIGI (gen. sg., "of Dubnorix") = "Nertomaros son of Dubnorix".

items.prompt: Why might the name VERCINGETORIX appear on a 1st-century CE funerary stone?
items.answer: Because the name lived on after the famous Vercingetorix's death. Gauls continued to name their children after him.

sections.body: Lesson 2.8 continues with funerary inscriptions, focusing on the genitive case: SEGOMARI MATIR ("mother of Segomaros"), DAXTIONI ATEPOMAROS ("Atepomaros son of Daxtio"), and the structure of Gaulish kinship terms.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can translate ANDEDASETI, MONI, MARKOM, and read all five inscriptions without hesitation.
